meta.scope: Large U.S. national and nationwide online banks with consumer savings products. Small local institutions excluded. This is a screened comparison, not a census of every bank.
meta.sourcePolicy: Use official bank product, rate, promotion, security, and FDIC pages for decision-critical values. Official search results may be used to locate official pages when the extractor omits dynamic content; linked current bank/regulator pages or disclosures support retained claims, and third-party rate data is never substituted. A value with no official support is null/blank and described in the review flags.

projection.formula: For elapsed calendar days d and APY r expressed as a percentage, estimated interest = P × ((1 + r/100)^(d/365) − 1). For sequential promotional periods, multiply the effective APY factors for each period. Horizons run from 2026-10-22 to the same calendar date 1, 3, or 5 years later.
assumptions: Account opening and initial funding are modeled as 2026-10-22; no account was actually opened.
Savings APYs are variable. The model holds each displayed APY constant for the period shown, which is a scenario, not a forecast or guarantee.
No withdrawals, recurring contributions, taxes, transfer delays, or account fees are included except where the SoFi Plus subscription fee is explicitly subtracted.
Promotional eligibility is conditional and must be met exactly; cash bonuses are shown separately from interest unless a row explicitly adds them.

The $250,000 FDIC reference is per depositor, per insured bank, per ownership category and includes principal plus accrued interest. Existing deposits at that bank/category are unknown and not modeled.
CIT's promotional and last-published standard-rate scenario is shown separately because its official APY disclosure is dated 2026-07-01, not 2026-10-22.
Rates are rounded as published. Banks may use daily-balance, leap-year, posting, and rounding conventions that produce small differences from these illustrative estimates.

Chase and Bank of America use location selectors; Citi's official page returned no numeric table; TD's displayed table cells were blank; Wells Fargo returned a California (ZIP 94105) view; U.S. Bank returned a ZIP 55402 view. Only values explicitly matched to a source location are retained, and no non-NYC rate is used in NYC projections.

flags.title: CIT Platinum Savings rate disclosure is dated 2026-07-01
flags.details: CIT's official product and BOOST50 pages display 3.75% standard / 4.25% promotional APY on balances of at least $5,000, but the APY accuracy date shown is July 1, 2026. The promo offer itself runs through December 15, 2026. Its value is included only as a clearly dated conditional scenario, not as a fresh October 22 standard rate.

flags.title: PNC High Yield Savings page title and body conflict
flags.details: The page title advertises an APY, but the current page body returned 'This Product Isn't Available in Your Area.' No numeric APY is treated as a confirmed, currently openable New York product; the comparison cell stays blank.

flags.severity: historical discrepancy resolved by current terms
flags.title: Marcus account-limit wording differs in an older agreement amendment
flags.details: The current Marcus FAQ and Deposit Account Agreement effective 2025-06-27 agree on a $3,000,000 aggregate account-owner limit and a general $1,000,000 per Online Savings/CD limit. A 2017 amendment contains historical new/legacy account-limit language; it is not used as the current rule. Recheck the current agreement during application. These bank limits do not increase FDIC insurance.

flags.severity: resolved for comparison, recheck at application
flags.title: Capital One rate extraction differs across official page paths
flags.details: Capital One's explicit account-comparison table lists 360 Performance Savings at 3.20% APY with no fees or minimums; its official footnote states rates effective 2026-10-21. The detailed account disclosure PDF dated 2026-07-15 also lists 3.20%, while an alternate extraction path rendered NaN. The explicit current comparison table is used and linked; confirm the APY on the application screen before opening.

flags.title: Savings APYs and public offers can change before or after opening
flags.details: Every projection holds published variable rates constant. It does not predict rate moves, guarantee a future APY, or assume an offer remains available after its stated end date. Re-open the official rate/terms link on the day of application.

flags.title: A $250,000 starting deposit has no room for interest under the standard single-category limit
flags.details: The FDIC limit includes accrued interest and aggregates same-bank deposits in the same ownership category. A $250,000 principal deposit can therefore exceed the standard limit as interest accrues, even if there are no other balances. Existing checking, savings, and CDs at the same legal bank can also use part of the same limit.

flags.title: SoFi's advertised additional deposit coverage is a separate program
flags.details: SoFi says its direct standard bank coverage remains subject to normal limits; additional coverage is through the separate Insured Deposit Program and participating banks. No additional-program coverage is counted in the standard comparison.

findings.baseline: At a $250,000 starting balance, Barclays Tiered Savings displays 3.65% APY at the $250,000+ tier (official APY date 2026-10-07); Synchrony displays 3.55% APY as of 2026-10-21 without a balance-tier or activity requirement. Barclays is the highest recently dated standard tier in this screened set, but its source is two weeks older and a $250,000 starting principal leaves no FDIC interest headroom.
findings.conditional: For eligible AARP members, Barclays Select Savings displays 4.25% APY and a separate $400 offer for $40,000 held under the stated terms through 2026-10-31. SoFi advertises 4.40% for up to six months with qualifying activity and separately up to $400 for eligible payroll/benefit/government direct deposits. Marcus referral adds 1.00 percentage point for three months. CIT BOOST50 displays 4.25% for six months at $5,000+, but the APY disclosure is dated 2026-07-01 and is flagged.
findings.recommendationFrame: There is no single unconditional winner for every depositor. Compare the no-activity Barclays/Synchrony choices against the conditional AARP, SoFi, Marcus, and CIT terms; account for fees, required balances, expiration dates, and FDIC aggregation before choosing.
findings.coverage: For single-owner deposits at one bank, keep principal plus accrued interest and all same-category deposits below $250,000 if full standard FDIC coverage is the goal. Brands or divisions sharing one legal bank do not create extra coverage.
